title: Vendor risk questionnaire walkthrough - Helio Insurance
topics: SOC 2 Type II and ISO status
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Helio through the SIG/CAIQ and their vendor risk questionnaire. Main asks: SOC 2 Type II report, encryption details (KMS), SSO/SAML & RBAC configuration, audit log retention and access, data residency options, and sample evidence for CAIQ answers. Agreed next steps to share SOC 2 + pen test summary, completed SIG spreadsheet, and schedule a follow-up to review evidence and contract redlines.

Jordan to send completed SIG/CAIQ spreadsheet (marked answers + evidence links) by 2025-07-25

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-21
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Alicia Gomez (Helio Security PM), Tom Becker (Helio IT Ops), Priya Sharma (Helio Procurement)

[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Uh this is Jordan from Redwood, along with Maya our systems engineer. How are you all?
[00:05] Alicia Gomez: Hi, thanks. Good. Ready to go. We circulated a vendor risk questionnaire ahead of time. We're mostly focused on SOC 2 evidence, SSO, and data residency.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Great, that's exactly what we wanted to cover. We'll walk through the SIG/CAIQ-style answers and point to evidentiary artifacts. We'll note where things are in progress like ISO, and where we have concrete artifacts like SOC 2 Type II.
[00:28] Priya Sharma: To be clear, procurement wants the completed questionnaire plus any supporting docs we can attach. Also any contract language about data residency.
[00:36] Jordan Patel: Yep, understood. Quick agenda: 1) SOC 2/ISO status and where you can find reports; 2) SIG/CAIQ walkthrough for controls you flagged; 3) SSO/SAML and RBAC specifics; 4) encryption/KMS and audit logs; 5) next steps and evidence handoff. Sound good?
[00:48] Tom Becker: Sounds good.

[02:10] Maya Chen: Starting with SOC 2 — Redwood currently has a SOC 2 Type II report covering Security and Availability for the period Jan–Jun 2025. We can provide the full report under NDA, plus a redacted summary for procurement. Our ISO 27001 is in progress; gap remediation is on track but not yet certified.
[02:35] Alicia Gomez: Okay can you confirm the scope? Is customer data in scope for SOC 2 and are we sure about hosted vs dedicated differences?
[02:42] Maya Chen: Good question — SOC 2 covers our hosted Redwood API and control plane operations; for Dedicated we have control mappings and we offer additional isolation and change controls. We'll flag which evidence maps to hosted vs dedicated.
[03:00] Jordan Patel: Practically speaking, if you plan to use Redwood Dedicated or Private, we can include deployment architecture diagrams and the Dedicated onboarding checklist as separate evidence.

[05:00] Maya Chen: Moving to the SIG spreadsheet, we went row-by-row for the client form you sent. There are a few rows we'll want to discuss: SSO (SAML 2.0) integration points, RBAC model (org/team/project roles), audit logging retention windows, and customer-managed keys for encryption.
[05:20] Alicia Gomez: For SSO we need confirmation of SAML metadata, SCIM support, and ability to enforce SSO-only login. Also we need role mapping so that we can limit admin access.
[05:33] Maya Chen: We support SAML 2.0 with IdP metadata exchange — yes. SCIM for user provisioning is supported; SCIM can be toggled per-org. You can enforce SSO-only via org policy; we also have role-based access controls where admin roles are separate from standard users. I'll point you to the docs and include a sample SAML metadata file.
[05:55] Priya Sharma: Is the RBAC enforced in the control plane or is it on the app layer? We need to know whether a user with admin at one org can see data for other orgs.
[06:04] Maya Chen: RBAC is enforced in the control plane; tenants are logically separated. Cross-org access only occurs via explicit admin delegation and is logged. So default non-admins have no cross-tenant visibility.

[08:10] Tom Becker: On encryption — can you outline key management? We have a policy that customer data keys must be KMS-backed and customer-owned keys preferred.
[08:20] Maya Chen: We support both platform-managed keys and customer-managed keys via KMS. For Hosted we offer integration with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) for envelope encryption around service-level keys. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can support bringing your own HSM. I'll share the architecture diagram and key rotation cadence.
[08:40] Jordan Patel: Note: when customers use CMK (customer-managed key), we document access procedures and the key usage logs are included in evidence.

[11:00] Alicia Gomez: Audit logs — what is retention and how granular are logs? We need to show login events, API request traces, and admin role changes for at least 12 months.
[11:12] Maya Chen: Default audit log retention is 90 days on hosted but we have an add-on for 12 months retention for customers under contract. For Dedicated/Private you can control retention locally. Logs include auth events, API request IDs, and admin role changes. We also provide exports and SIEM integration (syslog/ELK/CloudWatch).
[11:40] Priya Sharma: Is there an immutable log or WORM option? Our compliance team likes tamper-evident logs.
[11:47] Maya Chen: We don't provide a built-in WORM store on hosted by default, but we can configure log forwarding to an immutable store in your environment or support third-party WORM stores in Dedicated setups. We'll note that in the SIG answer.

[14:00] Jordan Patel: A few clarifying points from procurement: will the SOC 2 report be shared under an NDA, and do you have standard contract language for data residency and subprocessor disclosures?
[14:12] Maya Chen: Yes — SOC 2 and pen test reports are provided under NDA. We also have a standard Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and subprocessor list that we update monthly. We'll attach the current subprocessor roster.

[17:30] Tom Becker: On data residency — we need EU-only processing for some datasets. Does Redwood offer region pinning or dedicated EU-only deployments?
[17:40] Maya Chen: We offer region pinning on Hosted (EU region) and Dedicated capacity provisioned in customer-chosen regions. For strict EU-only processing with no outflow, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments; Hosted EU region still uses Redwood control plane in that region, and we can document data flows.
[18:00] Alicia Gomez: Can you provide contract language that commits to data residency?
[18:05] Jordan Patel: We can share templated contract clauses used in other customers and our DPA. Final language is typically negotiated but we can provide a starting point.

[20:00] Priya Sharma: A few items on the SIG: question 7.3 about encryption in transit and at rest — what exact ciphers and TLS versions do you support?
[20:10] Maya Chen: We support TLS 1.2 and 1.3 for in-transit. For at-rest we use AES-256-GCM for envelope encryption. We'll include the cryptographic spec doc. Note: some transcripts may show AES-256-GCM as AES-256-GCM-SHA but the point is AES-256.

[23:00] Alicia Gomez: Pen test details — are those internal tests or third-party? We need an independent report if available.
[23:08] Maya Chen: Our latest penetration test was performed by a third-party vendor QSec Labs in April 2025. We can provide an executive summary publicly and the full report under NDA.
[23:20] Jordan Patel: We'll attach the pen test exec summary to the SIG row and mark the full report as NDA-only.

[26:00] Tom Becker: For auditability — how do you prove separation of duties and change control for infra changes?
[26:10] Maya Chen: Change control is tied into our ticketing and review workflow; we have required approvals and pre/post change validation. We can provide our change management policy and sampled change tickets that are redacted.

[29:00] Priya Sharma: A question from procurement: what about subprocessor notification? We need 30-day notice of new subprocessors and the ability to object.
[29:10] Jordan Patel: Our DPA includes subprocessor notice terms and a process for objection; typical timeline is 30 days and we can surface critical subprocessors. We'll attach the DPA.

[31:30] Maya Chen: Quick demo of where to find artifacts — shared drive: https://redwood.example.com/security/ and I will upload SOC2-TypeII.pdf, pen-test-summary.pdf, SIG-completed-helio.xlsx. I'll also include a sample SAML metadata file and the RBAC diagram.
[31:55] Alicia Gomez: Great. When you upload the SIG spreadsheet can you annotate the evidence column with links and note which items are NDA-only?
[32:03] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll mark NDA-only and provide redacted artifacts where possible.

[35:00] Jordan Patel: A couple of risk questions we often see: data exfil possible vectors, backup encryption, and retention for backups.
[35:10] Maya Chen: Backups are encrypted at rest with customer or platform keys depending on deployment; retention is configurable, default 30 days for hosted backups, longer for Dedicated. Data exfil protections include VPC peering controls, Egress filtering, and monitoring with alerts for anomalous data transfers.

[38:00] Alicia Gomez: Is there a SOC 2 bridge letter or any continuous monitoring evidence we can use if the report period doesn't line up with our audit?
[38:10] Maya Chen: We can provide a SOC 2 bridge letter that outlines any material changes since the last audit period. For continuous monitoring we provide monitoring dashboards and can export relevant metrics.

[41:00] Priya Sharma: Any known outstanding findings from the last pen test?
[41:05] Maya Chen: There were low/medium findings that were remediated within our SLA window. We'll include the remediation notes in the pen test summary.

[43:30] Tom Becker: For the final SIG answer about encryption key custody, can you give a short sentence we can use in our vendor form?
[43:40] Maya Chen: Sure — suggested text: "Redwood supports platform-managed and customer-managed keys. For customer-managed keys, key material is stored in the customer's KMS and access is limited to cryptographic operations; key access is logged and auditable via KMS audit logs." We'll add that to the SIG cell.

[45:00] Jordan Patel: Quick recap of next steps: Maya uploads SOC 2 + pen test exec summary by Thursday 7/24; Jordan populates SIG and attaches evidence by Friday 7/25; Helio reviews and flags any follow-ups by 7/31; schedule follow-up the week of 7/28. Anything else?
[45:15] Alicia Gomez: We'd like sample contract clauses for data residency and subprocessor notice.
[45:20] Jordan Patel: We'll include DPA and suggested clauses.
[46:00] Priya Sharma: And one ask — can you include a short runbook for Dedicated deployment onboarding so security can see hardening steps?
[46:08] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll attach the Dedicated onboarding runbook and the hardening checklist.
[47:30] Alicia Gomez: Great thanks, appreciate it.
[47:35] Jordan Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the link to the shared folder and the SIG populated.
[47:40] Tom Becker: Thanks.
[47:45] Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains natural speech, occasional filler words, and a few minor transcription errors (e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache in an earlier auto transcript) — we corrected most but preserved the conversational tone. Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.example.com/security/SOC2-TypeII.pdf (NDA), https://redwood.example.com/security/pen-test-summary.pdf (NDA), https://redwood.example.com/security/SIG-completed-helio.xlsx (NDA).
